title: Active-gel BD twin replicates on seed 3: world keeps 9 comets with trails, local flow-free twins dissolve all peaks by t~27, the global twin leaves one fast body
summary: Fresh seed 3, t=200, the claim's world and the author's three twins. World: ~48 peaks at t=8 that thin out to 9 discrete comets with regulator trails by t~100 and persist to t=200 (world/sheet.png); 30 tracks >= 1 BL, max 9.2 BL, speed <= 0.52. Twin Lm=4: ~50 peaks at t=8 that blur away by t~27, then the field decays; 0 bodies at t=200 (twin_Lm4/sheet.png). Twin Lm=1: 0 bodies throughout. Global twin: 43 peaks reduce to 1 body by t=200, 7 tracks >= 1 BL, speed up to 2.85.

observations.F: world/sheet.png 9 persistent comets; twin_Lm4/sheet.png and twin_Lm1/FACTS.md 0 bodies; twin_global/FACTS.md 1 body at t=200

verdicts.limitation: One twin family (conversion toward screened stress); a twin with a different redistribution range or a slower inhibitor might keep peaks. The global twin's single body shows that discrete bodies are possible without transport when competition is global, so necessity is for a population of persistent bodies at local conservation.
